newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says agreed to buy 900,000 T Australia wheat.
newsitem.headline: Japan says agreed to buy 900,000 T Australia wheat.

text.p: Japan's Food Agency said on Wednesday it had agreed with the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) to buy about 900,000 tonnes of wheat in calendar 1997.
Prime Hard wheat will account for 200,000 tonnes of the total and the remaining 700,000 tonnes will be Australian Standard White, a senior official of the Food Agency told Reuters Wednesday evening.
The Food Agency and the AWB late last week agreed on the grain export quota, he said.
But the two sides failed to agree on a barley export quota for this year, the official said. He did not elaborate.
The Food Agency is the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry and is the sole importer of wheat, barley and rice. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk (+81-3-3432-7391)
